questions.stem: A monopoly is best defined as a market in which

options.text: a single firm supplies a commodity that has no close substitute
a few large firms supply the bulk of the market's output
many firms sell slightly differentiated products
there is only one buyer of a commodity

questions.explanation: Monopoly means one seller. The absence of a close substitute is just as important as the single seller, because if buyers could easily switch to another product the firm would have no real control over price.

distractorRationale.b: A few large firms dominating the market is oligopoly, not monopoly
distractorRationale.c: Many firms selling differentiated products describes monopolistic competition
distractorRationale.d: A single buyer is called a monopsony, which is a different concept

questions.stem: For a monopolist, the marginal revenue curve

options.text: lies above the average revenue curve
lies below the average revenue curve
coincides with the average revenue curve
is horizontal at the ruling market price

questions.explanation: To sell an extra unit the monopolist must cut price on every unit, not just the last one. The revenue gained from the extra unit is therefore reduced by the revenue lost on all the earlier units, so marginal revenue falls faster than price and lies below it.

distractorRationale.a: Marginal revenue can only exceed average revenue if price were rising as output rose, which contradicts the law of demand
distractorRationale.c: MR equals AR only when price is constant, which is the case of a price taker
distractorRationale.d: A horizontal MR curve belongs to perfect competition, where the firm faces a fixed price

questions.stem: A monopolist sells 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 units at prices of ₦100, ₦90, ₦80, ₦70 and ₦60 respectively. What is the marginal revenue, in naira, of the third unit?
questions.explanation: Total revenue at 2 units is 2 × ₦90 = ₦180 and at 3 units it is 3 × ₦80 = ₦240. Marginal revenue is the change in total revenue, ₦240 − ₦180 = ₦60. Notice this is less than the ₦80 price, because the price cut of ₦10 also applied to the two units already being sold.

questions.stem: Price discrimination by a monopolist is possible only if

options.text: the markets can be kept separate and have different elasticities of demand
the cost of producing the good differs between the two markets
the firm faces a horizontal demand curve
all buyers have identical incomes and tastes

questions.explanation: Separation stops buyers in the cheap market from reselling into the dear one, and different elasticities are what make two different prices worth charging — the higher price is loaded onto the market whose demand is more inelastic.

distractorRationale.b: If costs genuinely differ, charging different prices is not discrimination at all but simply cost-based pricing
distractorRationale.c: A horizontal demand curve means the firm is a price taker, which rules out discrimination completely
distractorRationale.d: Identical buyers would give identical elasticities, removing the very reason to discriminate

questions.stem: The supply of piped water to a city is usually left to one company because

options.text: water is not a scarce commodity
duplicating the pipe network would raise average cost enormously, making it a natural monopoly
the law forbids more than one company from selling any good
consumers prefer to buy from a government agency

questions.explanation: A natural monopoly arises where the fixed cost of the network is so large that one supplier serving the whole market produces at a much lower average cost than two suppliers each serving half. Laying a second set of pipes down every street would waste resources.

distractorRationale.a: Clean piped water is very scarce, which is precisely why its supply matters
distractorRationale.c: There is no such general law; monopoly is the exception, not the rule
distractorRationale.d: Consumer preference for a government agency is not the economic reason, and many water utilities are private

questions.stem: Which THREE of the following are measures a government can use to control monopoly?

options.text: Imposing a maximum price on the monopolist's product
Granting the monopolist a longer patent
Levying a tax on the monopolist's excess profit
Removing barriers to entry so that rivals can enter
Buying up all competing firms on the monopolist's behalf

questions.explanation: Price control caps exploitation directly, taxing excess profit transfers monopoly gains to the public, and removing entry barriers restores the competitive pressure that keeps price near cost. All three attack either the monopolist's price, its profit or its protection.

distractorRationale.b: A longer patent extends the legal barrier to entry and so strengthens monopoly power
distractorRationale.e: Buying up rivals is amalgamation, one of the ways monopolies are created in the first place

questions.stem: A monopolist can continue to earn abnormal profit in the long run.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Long-run profits are competed away only when new firms are free to enter. Barriers to entry are the defining feature of monopoly, so there is no mechanism to erode the abnormal profit and it can persist indefinitely.

distractorRationale.b: This confuses monopoly with perfect competition, where free entry drives long-run profit down to normal profit

questions.stem: Outline three sources of monopoly power and explain two disadvantages of monopoly to the consumer.
markingGuide: Legal grant: a patent, copyright or Act of parliament gives one firm the exclusive right to supply, as with the Central Bank of Nigeria's sole right to issue currency (2 marks)
Natural monopoly: a single large network such as water pipes or electricity transmission lines is far cheaper than duplicating it (2 marks)
Any one of: control of a scarce raw material, a very large capital requirement, superior secret technology, or amalgamation of all rivals (2 marks)
Disadvantage: output is restricted and price is set above marginal cost, so consumers pay more and consume less than under competition (2 marks)
Disadvantage: with no rival to fear, the monopolist may let quality and service fall, and consumers have no alternative supplier to turn to (2 marks)
questions.explanation: A full answer names the source of the barrier in each case rather than simply asserting that the firm is large. On the consumer side, the two strongest points are restricted output at a price above marginal cost, and the loss of quality and choice that follows from the absence of rivalry. Mentioning price discrimination against inelastic buyers earns credit too.
